Register a native UI extension in the selected cluster's Explorer navigation.

Use an expandable manager group with the application's name. Its label opens Overview and reveals the group, including when another child is active; keep disclosure controls distinct from route labels and follow native menu behavior.
Make Overview the default page and clearly indicate the active page.

Every manager ends with Pending Rollouts, Running Processes, Snapshots, Diagnostics, Settings, Help, in that order. Inventory pages and their dynamic resource entries precede this shared group. These common pages are specified here.

Prefer useful flat inventory pages; use nested expandable resource groups where relevant. Avoid redundant inventories. Create/Edit routes remain hidden from the sidebar and are reached through contextual actions.
Dynamic resource entries use stable identities, meaningful resource labels, and the active user's access, rather than positional indexes.

Use compact reactive count badges in a fixed left-hand column before menu labels. Align this column across top-level and nested entries; reserve blank space when there is no count. Disclosure arrows occupy a separate slot without shifting counts. Zone/domain entries show scoped record counts. An unavailable inventory is not zero.
Relevant page header, navigation, and Overview counts share the same scoped data; header counts sit immediately after Refresh. Example values are not fixed requirements.
Keep cluster identity visible and honor Rancher's cluster and namespace context.
Treat placement near Compliance as the Network Manager reference; validate ordering in the installed Rancher version rather than assuming a weight guarantees placement.
Target the recorded Rancher 2.15.x / Extensions API 3 environment initially; recheck compatibility when Rancher or the extension SDK changes.

Embedded pages inherit Rancher's active color scheme, theme tokens, typography, host viewport, and native left navigation. Use supported extension registration and routing rather than a second sidebar or global CSS overrides. Groups, nested entries, disclosure controls, selected routes, and namespace context follow the installed Rancher's menu behavior. Preview chrome is standalone-only. Validate requested count placement and loading indicators against native menu capabilities; a preview demonstration alone does not prove native navigation support.

Display counts only when they represent a relevant inventory or operation. Help and Settings have no counts. Reuse compact left-column navigation badges for domain/zone record counts, header counts, and other relevant inventories.

Use the DNS breadcrumb pattern: clickable manager name returns to Overview, followed by the current page; add clickable ancestors for nested editors where relevant. The manager title always opens Overview. Breadcrumbs and page headings use the same current route identity.

Zones is expandable/collapsible, with zone entries nested beneath it and record-count badges. Clicking its label opens the inventory; a separate arrow toggles children. Preserve active page, persisted order, counts, and expansion preference. Other inventory groups may use the same relevant pattern.

Every page-changing interaction synchronizes the active navigation item, including metric cards, grid/resource links, breadcrumbs, contextual Help, and editor actions. Hidden Create/Edit routes select their owning visible inventory item. Navigating to a child reveals its menu group; manual collapse may highlight the owning group while retaining the active child page. Do not highlight multiple unrelated items.

A count badge is red whenever a required dependency in that inventory/page scope is missing, unconfigured, unavailable, or failing. Explain the concrete blocking condition in its accessible description and tooltip, even when the item count is zero. Preserve the count's original meaning; do not substitute an incident total for a zone/record/item count. Optional or merely pending verification retains its appropriate separate state. Hiding a banner must not hide this required-failure indication. Diagnostics retains its warning/error event-count meaning.

Loading is a separate count-badge state: show a small spinner in the fixed count slot while the associated data is pending, rather than temporarily marking it red because readiness is not yet known. Preserve the last known count in its accessible description. Once the request resolves, show the actual count and health severity; a timeout/confirmed required failure is red. Keep the spinner aligned with other count badges and respect reduced-motion preferences.

The user's Network Manager screenshots define the shared layout, spacing, color, and presentation reference for every plugin page: [inventory grid](docs/design-reference/network-manager-port-configurations.png) and [Overview master/detail](docs/design-reference/network-manager-overview.png). Use the grid pattern for inventories and the master/detail pattern where useful; retain their common heading, status area, filters, panels, and aligned bottom edge. Screenshot data/counts are examples, not requirements to reproduce those values.
Reuse one page shell across pages and across the standalone preview/native extension.
Show manager name and cluster context, a clear page heading, a compact Help control, page-level actions, refresh controls, and an item count where useful.

Put all page actions, including Save/Save Draft, Test Connection, Cancel, selection-dependent actions, and manual refresh, in the top-right heading action row beside Refresh Every and its countdown. Modal confirmation controls remain within their dialog. Buttons in a group share width/height, padding, icon sizing, and alignment. Do not duplicate the page title inside its panel; retain distinct section headings where they communicate a separate subject.

Top-right actions that operate without a grid selection may appear whenever applicable. Any action that requires selected grid items stays hidden until items are explicitly selected; hide it again immediately when selection is cleared. This applies to Reorder, Delete, and every other selection-dependent operation, including applicable Merge, Apply, Reconfigure, Rescan, or Snapshot actions. Do not show a disabled button merely because no items are selected. Once items are selected, other unmet prerequisites may disable the action with an explanation. Create/New, Refresh, and editor actions use their own applicable context when they do not require grid selection.

Align heading actions with the primary title. New, Merge, Apply, and conditional red Delete share one font, icon size, and button height. The Network Manager reference uses 14 px text, 18 px SVGs, and 40 px buttons; Refresh stays icon-only.

Buttons within the same action group share dimensions, icon size, padding, font, border radius, and alignment. Use a common width for adjacent labeled actions sized for the longest label; changing primary/danger/secondary styling must not change geometry. Icon-only groups use consistent square hit areas, and their icons and controls align with neighboring actions.

Match Network Manager's shared buttons and refresh controls exactly by reusing its components and styles. Place Refresh Every, countdown, manual Refresh, and item count in the top-right heading action area, never in the filter/content row.
Position the item count immediately right of Refresh. Hover/focus help must render above navigation and avoid clipping; use a body overlay with bounded placement rather than click-only explanations.

Contextual Help/More Info uses an accessible circled question mark immediately beside its title, field, column, or status. Open a popup with Close and Open Help; reuse the relevant Help section. Open Help navigates to and expands that section. The Help page itself has no question-mark controls.
Keep the heading, status information, and filters outside the scrolling content area.
Fill the available viewport. Panels extend to the available bottom edge instead of stopping at an arbitrary content height.

The available viewport height is also the outer shell's maximum height. Account for Rancher's host chrome in native mode and the preview chrome in standalone mode; additional content must not expand the document into vertical page scrolling.
Use internal panel scrolling. In a master/detail view, align both panels to the same bottom edge; the list scrolls independently, and details scroll when content exceeds the panel.

Bound overflowing inventories, forms, and detail content to the remaining panel height and use the shared custom scrollbar styling. Keep headings, actions, and filters visible while that content scrolls.
Use `min-height: 0` / `min-width: 0` behavior in flex/grid content so long inventories do not push the shell beyond the viewport. Keep scrollbar gutters stable where appropriate.
Adapt layouts at smaller widths without clipping actions, filters, or dialogs.
Use consistent card borders, rounded corners, spacing, input heights, and form alignment. Align controls even when labels wrap onto multiple lines.

Inherit Rancher's active theme, tokens, typography, and host viewport in embedded pages; scope styles to the plugin. Standalone previews use the observed compact Network Manager dark presentation as their fallback.
Use thin dark scrollbars matching the panels. Preserve operating-system forced-color choices.
Keep collapsed sections visually connected with one divider between adjacent sections.
Use title case for button and status labels. Keep explanatory text concise and practical.
Use green for verified good/ready states, amber for pending/partial states, red for failures, and neutral styling for unknown or inapplicable states. Pair color with a readable label.

Status banners tint the entire banner background for their severity, matching Network Manager's full-width coverage notices. Pending/partial verification uses the amber/yellow warning surface, not only amber text or a colored border; errors use the corresponding error surface. Preserve readable contrast in both themes.
Keep badges and attachment counts compact and on one line. Enlarged badges should have a deliberate purpose rather than making every status compete with the page heading.

Use the whole amber warning background for pending/partial verification. Management backend unavailable is a full red error banner. Each top-of-page banner type has its own Settings visibility checkbox; hiding a banner does not change status or authorize writes.

Every yellow/amber warning or red error notification at the top of a page is clickable and keyboard accessible. Open the exact affected item's Create, Edit, or repair workflow directly, so the user can create, update, or fix it. Preserve cluster, namespace, resource identity, and relevant filter; select/reveal the item and prefill known context where applicable. Missing configuration opens its Create/setup flow; existing invalid configuration opens its Edit/fix flow. Multiple affected items open the scoped issue list with direct per-item fix actions. When the correction is external or no editor exists, open that item's specific diagnostic/recovery instructions. Avoid generic landing pages when a direct destination exists. Navigation must retain normal draft, authorization, review, snapshot, and confirmation gates; clicking the notification does not apply a fix. Other top-of-page alerts also open their relevant item/view or guide section.

subsection: Visual reference, not a mandatory pixel contract
requirement: The authenticated visual reference is `https://rancher.cormierconsulting.io`. Read-only inspection on 2026-10-11 found Lato 14 px typography and active tokens: body `#25282f`, body text `snow`, box `#171c22`, input `#25282f`, border `#38404b`, muted `#8f8f9c`, primary `#2f68df`, link `#9bbffd`. Embedded views consume these tokens dynamically; standalone previews use the observed theme as their fallback. Keep the normal host menu's group label and disclosure control separate, selected route behavior synchronized, and group expansion consistent with Rancher. Store this reference and observations, never credentials or copied authentication tokens.

Use automatic grid column widths. Only actual selection columns use narrow fixed widths; text columns must not inherit those widths. Align text and its header left, numeric values and their headers right. Counts, priority, TTL, and sizes use numeric sorting/alignment.
Sort file sizes by original bytes; use decimal B, KB, MB, GB, and TB units.
Provide an Overview summary plus searchable inventory and selected-resource details.

Use Rancher's existing top-level multi-select namespace filter as the single namespace control for embedded pages. Omit duplicate page-level namespace selectors and filter every inventory, overview, diagnostics view, operation, and relevant count from the host context directly. Match namespace/project/user/system/cluster scopes. Combine namespace selections as OR, with other page filters as AND. The standalone preview supplies one global namespace control in its simulated host header. Verify the native store contract.
Use searchable multi-select filters with a selected count, clear-selection action, and an understandable empty/default label. Dismiss popovers on Escape or outside interaction.
Combine selections with OR inside one filter and AND across different filter groups.
Include plugin-specific filters such as protocol, service/port configuration, zone, record type, component, severity, or generation source when applicable.
Search names and relevant identifiers, labels, destinations, and values. Document domain-specific search behavior in the plugin standard.
Show a Namespace column when namespace is part of the resource's identity; do not redundantly embed it in the displayed name. Show shared resources as Global.
Default configuration inventories to a flat list. Offer Group By Namespace where useful, placing Global first. Preserve shared configuration availability within relevant scopes.
Use a shared grid with sortable labeled columns, visible direction, numeric-aware comparisons, and accessible sort state. Do not sort selection/action columns.
Keep expanded detail rows attached to their parent during sorting and preserve group boundaries.
Retain headers on an empty grid and show a clear empty/no-matches message.
Clicking a configuration row opens read-only details. Action icons and selection checkboxes must not also toggle or select the row accidentally.
Keep row action icons right-aligned, horizontal, and unwrapped, with consistent compact hit areas, tooltips, accessible names, and visible keyboard focus.

Add selection checkboxes and Select All only to full inventory grids with meaningful selection actions. Compact/embedded tables, summary panels, cards, and detail lists do not gain checkboxes merely to make them selectable. Use normal row/card activation for details; when selecting in a full grid, apply the displayed scope.

Explicit grid selection reveals applicable selection-dependent contextual buttons in the top-right page action area, including Reorder and Delete. Hide them with no selected items; merely opening/highlighting a details-only row is not grid selection. Hide inapplicable actions and explain other unmet prerequisites when disabling an action for an existing selection. Derive the action's affected scope from the explicit selection and show it in review; never silently affect unselected resources. Contextual buttons use the same dimensions, icon size, padding, and alignment as neighboring actions. Selecting a details-only row must not implicitly authorize a mutation.

Use the DNS Manager preview's native checkbox presentation as the shared checkbox reference, superseding older Network Manager checkbox styling. Use real checkbox inputs with consistent size, theme, selection-column placement, spacing, and vertical alignment in headers and rows; do not substitute decorative checkbox icons. Keep checked, unchecked, disabled, focus, and partial-selection states clear. Select All reflects the displayed authorized scope and is indeterminate for a partial selection. Give every checkbox an accessible label and preserve keyboard interaction; selecting it must not also open row details. Reorder mode replaces these controls with handles according to the shared ordering standard.
Review the exact affected resources before a bulk delete; preserve unrelated objects and Secrets.
Distinguish observed resources, working drafts, validated pending proposals, and examples in both labels and counts. Inferred associations must not be presented as durable ownership.

Match the user's [filter-row reference](docs/design-reference/network-manager-filter-row.png): labels above the controls, consistent control height/borders/padding, a leading disclosure arrow for multi-select namespace choices, and evenly spaced columns aligned along their control bottoms. Diagnostics orders these as Search, Lookback (hours), Log source, Severity on one row when space permits. Controls fill their columns and wrap responsively rather than clipping or changing size.

Put **Reorder** in the top-right page action area when manual ranking is supported and grid items are selected, following the shared selection-dependent visibility rule. Delete follows the same rule; Create remains independent of selection.

Normal mode shows row selection checkboxes; Reorder appears only with an explicit selection. Entering reorder mode replaces every row's selection checkbox with a drag handle and removes the Select All control. Selection enables entry into the ordering workflow; the complete authorized collection remains its reviewed scope.
Clicking Reorder hides the Reorder button and shows Cancel in that action area. Create/Delete and bulk selection are unavailable while ordering is being edited.
Entering reorder mode alone does not show Save. Show Save beside Cancel only when the proposed order differs from the persisted order. Moving rows back to the original order hides Save again.
Support drag-and-drop ordering and a keyboard-accessible equivalent using the same handles. Show the intended drop position and keep the moved row's details attached to it.

During reorder mode, the whole row is a drag target: users can grab it anywhere, not only by its handle. Keep the handle as a visual cue and keyboard control; suppress normal row navigation/selection while dragging and retain Cancel/Save semantics.
Capture the persisted order and its revision on entry, and edit a separate local proposal. Dropping a row changes only that proposal; it must not write through automatically.

Reorder the complete authorized collection in persisted priority order. Suspend table sorting, grouping, filtering, and pagination that would conceal or rearrange members during editing; do not silently renumber rows outside the user's writable scope.

Cancel discards the proposed order, restores the persisted order and normal controls, and writes neither ordering configuration nor a rollout. Existing selection/view context may be restored for items that still exist. Guard navigation away from a changed proposal like any other form.

Refresh may update status information but must not replace a proposed order. If membership, permissions, or the persisted revision changes, mark the proposal conflicted and require review against the current collection before saving; never silently overwrite concurrent changes.

Save reviews the previous/proposed order and affected scope, then stages the ordering draft in Pending Rollouts. Apply there uses the standard snapshot flow: validate or capture a recent matching snapshot of persisted configuration, confirm storage, recheck coverage/revision, and persist the complete ordering configuration through the backend. Include stable IDs, order/ranks, scope, and revision.

Use the existing 24-hour/full-coverage snapshot requirement for this configuration change. A browser-only reorder is not a successful save. Capture the old order, not the unsaved proposal, as the pre-change recovery state; store the proposed order separately in the change record.

While saving, prevent duplicate submission and further dragging. Leave the proposal available with an error if validation, backup, or persistence fails. Do not report success before backend acknowledgment.

After staging Save, return to normal mode, restore checkboxes, and recalculate action visibility from the current selection; Reorder/Delete stay hidden when nothing is selected. Hide Save/Cancel; active navigation retains the applied order. Update navigation only after Apply confirms persistence. The applied order must survive reloads and manager/backend restarts and be included in snapshot restoration.

Support two Overview design variants within the shared shell: **Summary** (DNS Manager's metric cards followed by flow/status and summary panels) and **Master/Detail** (Network Manager's metric cards and filters above a left selectable inventory and right details panel). These are reusable design patterns, not a requirement for an application to offer a runtime layout switch. Keep the current DNS Summary arrangement; choose the variant appropriate to the application.
Each Overview variant supports keyword search across relevant names, namespaces, and identifiers, and consumes the single host namespace filter from section 4.
Use compact statistic cards for actionable inventory, errors, related resources, and pending changes.
Clicking an actionable card opens the corresponding page with the relevant filter.
Overview exposes resumable working drafts and validated pending changes distinctly.
Present the configured flow and resource context together where the application has a flow. Do not imply configured references prove successful traffic or service availability.
Resource context includes namespace, owning application/controller, and applicable change state.
Link Kubernetes resources to their native Rancher detail pages in the active cluster.

Namespace, workload, pod, Service, node, Secret-reference, and other Rancher resource references are clickable native detail links wherever a destination can be resolved. Use active cluster context and stable resource identity; standalone previews use the configured Rancher URL. Disclose unavailable destinations rather than rendering misleading links; show Secret metadata only.
Deep links into history/snapshots retain the selected resource scope and provide Clear Filter.
Use collapsible detail sections to keep the default view readable; define domain-specific sections and their default expansion in the plugin standard.
Open concrete HTTP/HTTPS address links in a new tab. Wildcards, regular expressions, raw TCP/SNI, and UDP addresses are references, not fabricated web URLs.
Show internal Service addresses and forwarded endpoint addresses separately; resolve named ports from actual metadata, bracket IPv6 addresses, and explain unavailable/headless addresses.
Address display is not a reachability check. Show the observation time/source when applicable.
Reuse form spacing, labels, help, validation feedback, and action placement across editors.
Start each new-resource editor with a clean form. Preserve context for intentional edits.
Keep immutable identity fields locked on existing resources.
Retain user-entered names and overrides. Provide an explicit Use Suggested Name action rather than overwriting a customized name when another selection changes.
Populate dependent selectors from inventory and the selected profile/scope.
Inline Add actions may create related drafts; distinguish these from persisted live resources.
Validate dependencies, incompatible options, missing references, and conflicting mappings before creating a rollout proposal. Repeat authoritative validation on the server before writes.
Offer Save Draft And Leave, Discard Changes, and Stay On This Page when navigation would lose unsaved changes. Cover both the plugin's controls and native Rancher route changes.
Allow incomplete working drafts to be resumed from Overview. Explain their persistence lifetime.
Keep Cancel beside the other form actions as an outlined/secondary button.
Refresh must preserve field values, active drafts, selection, and the editor instance.
Distinguish saving a draft from publishing/applying it. Disable live actions without a working, authenticated backend; saving local state must not claim a live resource was changed.

Integration editors that configure a connection provide **Test Connection** using the current unsaved settings. Show the tested scope, result, and observation time; invalidate the result when connection settings change. Distinguish network reachability from authentication and the required service operations. Testing does not save or mutate managed configuration, and a missing backend cannot report a successful test.

section: 7. Pending rollouts, processes, and change review
requirement: Separate incomplete working drafts from validated pending rollout proposals.

section: 7. Pending rollouts, processes, and change review
requirement: All unapplied managed changes are saved as drafts and visible in Pending Rollouts, including incomplete drafts labeled Needs Completion. Validate a draft into a reviewable proposal before enabling Apply. A form save stages the change without applying it. Apply from Pending Rollouts starts the backend operation, visible in Running Processes with its actual state and results. This includes ordering and configuration changes: the snapshot/revision gate runs before execution, and active navigation reflects confirmed configuration rather than an unapplied draft. Local display preferences and non-mutating tests do not create rollouts.

section: 7. Pending rollouts, processes, and change review
requirement: Collect relevant creates, edits, reissues, configuration changes, deletions, and restore proposals in one review location. Repeated saves replace the same proposal rather than duplicating it.

section: 7. Pending rollouts, processes, and change review
requirement: Provide the affected resource list, scope, current/proposed configuration, and downloadable manifests or equivalent native configuration before application.

section: 7. Pending rollouts, processes, and change review
requirement: Keep the pending counter shared between navigation and Overview. Examples do not count as changes.

section: 7. Pending rollouts, processes, and change review
requirement: For reusable configurations, show affected consumers before updating them. Editing a preset alone does not silently update existing consumers; reconfiguration is an explicit reviewed operation.

section: 7. Pending rollouts, processes, and change review
requirement: Validate the complete affected group before applying it. Aim for consistent group changes and report partial failures truthfully when the backend cannot provide transactions.

section: 7. Pending rollouts, processes, and change review
requirement: Detect concurrent edits or changed dependencies and require a fresh review instead of overwriting them.

section: 7. Pending rollouts, processes, and change review
requirement: Detect Helm/Fleet/controller ownership and route edits through the owning source or clearly explain the reconciliation consequence before enabling a conflicting mutation.

section: 7. Pending rollouts, processes, and change review
requirement: Track submitted work on the required Running Processes page, including operation, namespace/scope, status, start time, affected resources, progress when known, and configuration details.

section: 7. Pending rollouts, processes, and change review
requirement: Do not invent progress percentages or completion. Label simulated processes as simulations.

section: 7. Pending rollouts, processes, and change review
requirement: Keep session rollout/rollback history distinct from durable configuration snapshots.

Store snapshots in a dedicated persistent server location, outside rotating logs. Confirm backend storage before satisfying any backup gate. Keep the volume in an independent backup policy; replication/persistence alone is not a backup.

Export ZIP files containing the configuration index and independently readable manifests/configuration. Include Secrets is an explicit checkbox, default off; non-secret configuration is always included. A second downloaded copy is optional; a download-only workflow requires acknowledgment that the files were saved.

Capture persisted pre-change configuration separately from local proposals and declared dependencies. Include Secret manifests/values only with Include Secrets; otherwise retain references and disclose omitted credential coverage. Exclude application/PV data. List unavailable Secrets and the observation time.

Both Create Snapshot and the snapshot schedule's Run Now first open a modal asking whether to Include Secrets (default off). Selecting Include Secrets shows Password and Confirm Password fields and a locally evaluated strength bar beneath the password field. Show a readable strength label and mismatch feedback, with accessible labels/focus. Confirm requires matching passwords and the shared strength policy; Cancel clears both passwords and returns Include Secrets to unchecked.

Secret-inclusive backups require password encryption of the entire backup payload, including the index, configuration, and Secret manifests. Use AES-256 encrypted ZIP entries through a maintained implementation, not legacy ZipCrypto or a UI-only password check. Keep all recovery content in one encrypted payload entry (for example backup.zip inside the outer ZIP) with a generic filename, because ordinary ZIP encryption leaves entry names/metadata visible. See [WinZip encryption format](https://www.winzip.com/en/support/aes-encryption/) and [ZIP directory visibility](https://kb.winzip.com/en/130859).

Passwords are transient capture/export inputs: do not place them in drafts, browser storage, logs, or the archive index. Clear them on completion/cancellation. Never emit an unencrypted Secret-inclusive file when encryption fails. Verify that correct-password recovery succeeds and wrong/missing-password access fails before treating encrypted backup creation as successful.

Secret references alone are not restorable credentials. Redact Secret values and annotation values in all on-screen comparisons, including last-applied annotations; retain full captured manifests only within appropriately protected recovery content.

Provide listing, search, scope/generation filters, manual capture, downloads, uploads, inspection, comparison, selected restoration with dependencies, merge, protected backup deletion, automatic scheduling, and retention cleanup.
Default to Created descending using raw timestamps, including within namespace groups and on a fresh open. Refresh preserves an explicit user-selected sort.

Size sorts numerically by the complete stored/exported ZIP bytes and uses decimal B, KB, MB, GB, and TB. Legacy JSON/YAML pairs display their combined byte size explicitly; they do not supply the complete-ZIP size used by current capacity estimates.

Use the common header actions/help/refresh/count shell. New uses a plus; Delete uses a red trash action with matching geometry. Scope filters include Manual or Automatic generation and date ranges with calendar selection, optional times, Clear Range, and convenient start-to-end selection.

For reconfiguration, rollback, restoration, bulk deletion, and ordering changes, verify a matching snapshot captured within the previous 24 hours for the complete affected configuration. Recheck coverage, age, and revisions at execution time. Changes invalidate coverage; a recent timestamp alone is insufficient.

Select a stored snapshot or upload its index; automatically compare saved/current affected content side by side. YAML alone does not establish capture age or scope. Mismatching configuration cannot satisfy the mutation gate.

Restoration reviews affected items/dependencies and what will be overwritten. Require a fresh current-state snapshot and explicit overwrite confirmation. Block uncovered consumers, missing dependencies, and newer conflicting edits.

Require explicit Secret selection/confirmation for credential replacement. Managed resource deletion never removes Secrets. Never silently restore unrelated objects or remove resources created after the selected snapshot.
Prepare restoration drafts in Pending Rollouts; Apply is a separate reviewed backend operation tracked in Running Processes. Preserve capture provenance.
Provide recovery instructions for obtaining files without the application and restoring reviewed native configuration, including owning Helm/Fleet sources.

Begin with Verify Snapshot Passwords when preparing selected sources. List every protected snapshot with its own password input, a Test Password action, and an adjacent Apply To All Snapshots action. Applying a password never verifies it. Provide Test All Passwords and show actual archive-decryption results per snapshot. Editing or copying passwords invalidates prior verification. Reverify before continuing; do not rely on a nonempty field or cached success alone.

Warn explicitly which snapshots will not be processed and why (missing password, incorrect password, unreadable archive). Include unencrypted snapshots normally. Only protected snapshots with a successfully supplied password enter the merge; skipped snapshots never enter priority, selection, provenance, output, or source deletion. Require at least two eligible sources. Keep the exclusion warning through final review. Passwords remain only in session memory and are never saved in drafts, preview source files, browser storage, logs, or exported metadata.

Merge opens a dedicated page in the shared shell. Its navigable stepper is Override Priority, one selection step per relevant item type, Review Differences, Final Summary. Each plugin adapter supplies its item types, selection order, stable identities, and dependency relationships in its own standard.

Highest-priority sources override lower ones by stable item identity, taking a complete item from the winning source; missing items come from lower sources. Support drag ordering and accessible keyboard controls.

Every selection step shows only additions/content changes. Matching items remain in the final backup automatically. Skip types with zero additions/changes; a fully matching merge goes directly from priority to review and final confirmation.
Automatically include known required dependencies; block unresolved dependencies. Keep selection, comparison, summaries, and backup output consistent.

Changed Secrets default to keeping readable current credentials; selecting a snapshot version requires an explicit choice. Read current versions of every source Secret as well as currently referenced Secrets, including after references change. Failed reads cannot silently reuse stale credentials. If current values are unavailable, preserve the saved version in the backup and disclose the gap. Matching Secrets keep their original capture provenance. Merge never writes live credentials and follows the same Include Secrets/encryption contract as capture.

Compare the effective flattened selection against current configuration, side by side, showing additions/content changes only. Shared IDs alone are not conflicts; matching and current-only items are excluded and never implicitly deleted. Ignore transient controller status/resource-version changes in comparisons.

Final confirmation states scope, precedence, added/changed counts, and whether originals are retained. Offer Remove These Snapshots When Merged; partial merges that omit configuration retain originals. Save durably before any source removal. Cleanup failure leaves a successful save intact and permits separate cleanup without retrying the merge. Preserve per-item capture dates through merges and subset selection: merging old content does not make its coverage fresh.
Protect unsaved merge choices using the common draft/leave guard and register the merge editor as a hidden route. Merging, restoration preparation, and Apply remain separate actions.

Show per-resource coverage and snapshot history. The coverage display checks the last seven days: green matching, amber partial/differing, red no recent applicable copy. This display window is separate from the 24-hour mutation gate. Multiple snapshots may collectively cover known configuration; fixtures do not prove live backup.

Make the banner clickable and keyboard accessible. Green opens the inventory; partial/missing/outdated coverage opens a dedicated summary/diff page using the Snapshots shell. Group missing, outdated, and changed items into collapsible sections by type; hide matching/recently covered items. Compare uncovered items with their latest applicable stored version, redacting Secret values.

For this notification only, Secrets use backup presence rather than freshness or content differences. A Secret with captured values in an applicable stored backup is excluded from freshness/difference totals, even after rotation. References without captured values remain missing-backup gaps, including with Include Secrets off. Record missing/omitted recovery coverage in the index and recovery comments. This presence-only rule never relaxes restore dependencies or write validation.
Resource history links retain selected scope and provide Clear Filter. Network Manager defines its resource-specific badge layout in its own standard.

Place Automatic Snapshot Schedule and Automatic Snapshot Cleanup side by side at the bottom, each occupying 50% of the row. Align configuration fields left, actions right, and use compact retention units. Beneath each panel's controls show only its next date: Next Snapshot in the capture panel and Next Delete in the cleanup panel. Put explanatory/status paragraphs about server scheduling, browser closure, capture source, recovery copies, retention protection, and estimation assumptions in a help icon beside the corresponding panel title, linking to the relevant guide section. Errors remain visible and actionable.
Enabled is a green badge; Disabled is red. Loading/unknown has a distinct state.

Persist enabled state, interval, scope, and capture source on the server; run with the browser closed. Support minutes, hours, days, weeks, and calendar months with month-end clamping. Disclose whether the source is fresh live state or saved inspection.
Cleanup is disabled by default. Protect the newest applicable snapshot for each known scope/configuration item and retain originals required by partial merges.

Immediately below both panels, provide a separate row spanning 100% of the combined width, divided into three equal columns: Available Drive Space, Largest Snapshot, and Estimated Run Out Of Space. No storage figures belong inside either schedule panel. Format examples (illustrative, never hardcoded): `Available Drive Space: 950.8 GB / 1.1 TB`; `Largest Snapshot: 555.6 KB · Approximately 1,711,350 More Snapshots Fit`.

Available storage means bytes writable by the service account at the configured destination: available filesystem space bounded by any smaller remaining PVC, dataset, volume, tenant, or application quota. Do not show parent drive capacity as backup capacity or double-count replicas. Required limits that cannot be measured show Unavailable with a reason, never zero or a fabricated exhaustion date.

Measure the actual mounted filesystem containing the resolved snapshot-save directory (including PVC/bind mounts/symlinks); report effective available bytes and that destination's total capacity. Do not substitute the host's root disk, browser disk, or a different mount. Apply smaller known quotas and disclose them through contextual Help. Refresh from backend measurements rather than fixtures.

Estimates use the largest complete saved ZIP, effective available bytes, and the saved enabled cadence. Without a size or enabled schedule, show no prediction. Explain competing usage and cleanup assumptions in contextual Help rather than helper paragraphs. Refresh measurements in place after capture, cleanup, schedule changes, and normal refresh. An estimate is not a promise of available capacity.

If the computed exhaustion date is more than one calendar year from the measurement time, display `∞` instead of a distant date; retain the full estimate for accessible help. At exactly one year or sooner, show the localized date/time. Unknown size, unavailable space, or a disabled schedule remain Unavailable or Not Scheduled as appropriate; never turn unknown estimates into infinity.
Provide a shared manual Refresh action and Refresh Every selector.
Default to five minutes. Offer Off, 30 Seconds, 1 Minute, 5 Minutes, 15 Minutes, and 1 Hour.
Show a fixed-width `MM:SS` countdown driven by a clock deadline, avoiding accumulated timer drift. Interval changes and manual refresh reset it; Off displays `00:00`.
Update data in place without page reloads, editor remounts, or replacement of unsaved form state.
Prevent overlapping refresh work. Show busy/error feedback and retain existing data on failure.

For a delayed data request (300 ms default), show a centered loading indicator over a blurred/dimmed page with an accessible loading status. Preserve the underlying editor and data rather than remounting them. Fail an unanswered request after 60 seconds with a visible timeout message; retry failed reads every 60 seconds except confirmed source disconnections, which retry every five seconds and restore the regular five-minute refresh after verified recovery. Show count spinners only during delayed requests; confirmed failures remain red between attempts. Retry until successful or cancelled. Show the retry countdown, prevent overlapping requests, abort abandoned requests, and ignore late responses. Clear the overlay on response/cancellation. Do not automatically replay timed-out rollout writes; reconcile their backend operation status before any explicit retry.

Reserve loading indicators for actual delayed requests (300 ms default); idle, unconfigured sources and retry countdowns are not loading. Keep confirmed failures visible between attempts. Missing configuration requires configuration, not probes.

Diagnostics follows Network Manager's filter layout with keyword search, multi-select namespace scope from Rancher's global selector, log source, severity (Debug, Info, Warn, Error), and lookback. Discover relevant running resources and controller replicas as sources via the backend, and label unavailable collections distinctly. The navigation badge counts only warnings/errors over the rolling last 24 hours, independent of view filters: neutral zero, yellow warnings-only, or red combined warnings and errors when any error exists. Identify scope (browser vs managed-resource logs).
Diagnostics defaults to a 24-hour view. Each adapter documents its available retention/lookback limits in its plugin standard.

Make badge scope, time window, and separate severity counts accessible. Keep its rolling 24-hour total independent of view filters while honoring host namespace/access scope. Unavailable log data is not a verified zero.
Clearly label demo logs, static inventory, simulated operations, and unverified observations. A refresh of static/demo data must not claim a fresh live cluster inspection.

Persist display preferences per browser, including Preview, snapshot status banner, and cluster inspection notices as separate controls. These controls change presentation, not access or write capability.

Every top-of-page notification/banner type has its own labeled visibility checkbox in Settings. New banner types must add the matching preference rather than relying on a single global hide switch. Apply preferences consistently across pages and persist them per browser; hiding a banner does not alter underlying status or bypass required validation, backup, or write controls.

Default Preview off for standalone test builds and native extension builds. An explicit saved preference may enable preview labels and banners; fresh root-suite sessions start with them off. This preference changes presentation only. Hidden notices do not turn sample data into live evidence, disable mock data, or suppress real issue notifications.
Standalone resource links may use a configured Rancher origin, validated as an HTTP/HTTPS origin without embedded credentials. Native builds use the active Rancher context.
Provide the Rancher URL and other relevant connection/configuration settings on the shared Settings page, alongside per-banner visibility preferences.

Help is the final navigation page and has no inventory count or question-mark controls. Use collapsible sections for the application's purpose, every page, action, resource link, and common workflow; describe each trigger and effect.

Explain preview versus live capabilities and how to recover or diagnose failures. Contextual popups reuse these sections; Open Help navigates to and expands the relevant section. Help's application links open the page/section they describe and synchronize the active navigation item.

section: 10. Authentication, availability, packaging, and implementation boundaries
requirement: Reuse Rancher's authenticated session and enforce the active user's permissions for both reads and writes. Loading an authenticated UI is not sufficient backend authorization.

section: 10. Authentication, availability, packaging, and implementation boundaries
requirement: Keep backend credentials and private keys out of browser state, repository files, plaintext exports, and logs. The explicit Include Secrets encrypted-backup flow is the exception for recovery exports; never display its values in the UI. Show Secret reference names/keys rather than Secret values.

section: 10. Authentication, availability, packaging, and implementation boundaries
requirement: Read public certificate metadata only; do not return private keys or provider credentials.

section: 10. Authentication, availability, packaging, and implementation boundaries
requirement: The plugin manages configuration; managed routing/DNS must continue if its UI or management API fails.

section: 10. Authentication, availability, packaging, and implementation boundaries
requirement: Use versioned extension assets and a Helm chart registering `UIPlugin`. Publish the Rancher `files.txt` plus `plugin/` layout, not merely a standalone JavaScript URL.

section: 10. Authentication, availability, packaging, and implementation boundaries
requirement: Separate UI registration, asset hosting, management backend, and managed workloads. Clearly document which chart installs which resources; registration alone does not install those dependencies.

section: 10. Authentication, availability, packaging, and implementation boundaries
requirement: Reuse existing infrastructure rather than adding another ingress, database, or monitoring stack merely to support a manager page.

section: 10. Authentication, availability, packaging, and implementation boundaries
requirement: A standalone preview uses the same components with isolated fixture data and clearly declared capabilities. Keep unauthenticated preview hosting private and free of live cluster credentials.

section: 10. Authentication, availability, packaging, and implementation boundaries
requirement: Every custom Rancher plugin must include a repository-owned, locally runnable standalone interface preview. An inline mockup alone does not satisfy this requirement.

section: 10. Authentication, availability, packaging, and implementation boundaries
requirement: Match the Network Manager development workflow: `npm install` (or `npm ci` with the lockfile), `npm run preview`, and `npm run build:preview`. Pin dependencies and retain the lockfile.

section: 10. Authentication, availability, packaging, and implementation boundaries
requirement: `npm run preview` must start a usable browser-based plugin UI directly from the local project after dependency installation. It must work without Docker or Docker Compose, container image builds, a full application deployment, or a Kubernetes/Helm installation. Optional container/backend integration previews may supplement this npm workflow but cannot replace it or become prerequisites. Use clearly labeled fixtures/local adapters for unavailable services so pages, navigation, forms, selection actions, and draft flows can be previewed locally.

section: 10. Authentication, availability, packaging, and implementation boundaries
requirement: Document the preview URL, prerequisites, commands, and how to stop it with Ctrl+C. Bind to `127.0.0.1` by default and use a documented, distinct port so managers can run together. Network Manager uses 5173; DNS Manager uses 5174. Fail clearly on a port conflict.

section: 10. Authentication, availability, packaging, and implementation boundaries
requirement: Each plugin folder supports `npm run preview`; repository-root `npm run preview` launches all registered plugins together for cross-plugin consistency checks. Support choosing named plugins and stop only processes started by that run. Present the selected plugins in one browser page, with side-by-side and full-width views that retain each plugin's active state. Prepopulate one temporary project-owned session datasource using the shared contract, with separate logical plugin records and snapshot directories. Saves persist within that session without changing the seed fixtures; retain session files after stopping. Start preview-only labels and banners disabled, while identifying mock data in the suite shell. This display preference must not disable mock data or real issue notifications.

section: 10. Authentication, availability, packaging, and implementation boundaries
requirement: Use one shared datasource contract for normalized inventory, saved state, refresh, capabilities, and reviewed writes. Project-owned JSON mock sources are editable and saveable through npm previews, including provenance/schema information. Persist valid edits atomically with revision conflict checks and visible failures. Native Rancher API adapters implement the same contract through authenticated reads and reviewed writes; changing providers must not require rewriting page UI. Credentials, passwords, and decrypted Secret values must never enter mock files.

section: 10. Authentication, availability, packaging, and implementation boundaries
requirement: Every feature and ability must have representative demo data pulled from its authoritative source where available, scrubbed before persistence, and saved in one project-owned global local demo database/data file shared by the plugin suite. Include the states needed to exercise the feature, such as populated and empty inventories, dependencies, drafts, warnings, errors, and operation results. Preserve source identity, capture time, schema version, and the scrubbing rules; label synthetic scenarios and never present them as live observations. Remove real credentials, Secret values, private keys, personal information, and sensitive identifiers; use safe replacements that retain referential consistency. Track and synchronize the global demo file with Git LFS and include its tracked pointer in the repository, so a normal checkout with LFS provides the prepopulated data. Document LFS setup/pull and report missing LFS content clearly. Root and per-plugin npm previews consume this same global source through the swappable datasource contract; preview saves use editable local/session copies rather than overwrite the distributed seed. A new feature is incomplete until its representative data, scrub/validation checks, and UI tests are included.

section: 10. Authentication, availability, packaging, and implementation boundaries
requirement: Keep the standalone Rancher-like shell outside native integration; reuse the manager's Vue page components for the preview and native routes. Native pages use Rancher's own chrome.

section: 10. Authentication, availability, packaging, and implementation boundaries
requirement: Interface preview startup must not require cluster credentials, Windows connectivity, the managed service, a live management backend, or any Docker/test containers. Label sample inventory and simulated status. Document browser-only preview state separately from backend-confirmed durable snapshots.

section: 10. Authentication, availability, packaging, and implementation boundaries
requirement: Keep preview/build, publication, installation, and live execution distinct. Do not describe a generated draft or compiled library as deployed functionality.

section: 10. Authentication, availability, packaging, and implementation boundaries
requirement: Verify native integration, authorization, live observation, server validation, and result readback before marking a live feature implemented.

section: 10. Authentication, availability, packaging, and implementation boundaries
requirement: Deliver an installable Helm-based package that deploys the application's runtime and registers its Rancher management interface in the native left navigation. Build the actual extension bundle, page routes, Explorer menu registration, and operator-compatible extension chart; a generic workload chart or Vite preview alone does not register a Rancher UI extension. Declare the compatible Rancher version and required extension operator/CRDs. When Rancher's management cluster and workload cluster differ, explicitly target both: a Helm release only creates resources in its target cluster. Keep one documented installation workflow without claiming a single ordinary release can implicitly configure another cluster. Release acceptance includes a clean Helm install, visible native menu/routes, theme/namespace integration, refresh recovery, upgrade, and uninstall checks. See [Rancher's extension packaging](https://extensions.rancher.io/extensions/v2/publishing) and [native side-menu registration](https://extensions.rancher.io/extensions/next/api/nav/side-menu).

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] Native group opens Overview; menus, resource identities, and counts use the correct context.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] Shared heading/actions/help, viewport layout, internal scrolling, and responsive behavior work.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] Grids sort correctly, retain empty headers, and keep expanded rows with their parent.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] Filters/search/grouping honor scope; icon actions do not accidentally toggle rows.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] Top-right selection-dependent actions, including Reorder/Delete, are hidden without explicit grid selection and disappear when selection is cleared.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] Ranked collections use the shared top-right Reorder/Cancel/dirty-only Save flow; order persistence, conflict detection, snapshot recovery, and related navigation are verified.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] Keyboard navigation, labels, focus, dialogs, and non-color status descriptions are usable.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] New/edit forms preserve intentional overrides and guard unsaved navigation.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] Refresh keeps drafts/selection intact and accurately identifies source/freshness.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] Working drafts, validated proposals, submitted processes, examples, and durable snapshots are distinct.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] Changes expose affected resources, ownership, before/after review, and concurrency validation.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] Applicable mutation gates verify recent full-scope backup and recheck before execution.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] Snapshots survive application restart and support recovery without the manager.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] Schedules/cleanup run with the browser closed, disclose source, and protect retained coverage.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] ZIP/Include Secrets encryption, recovery, provenance, merge, and presence-only banner rules work.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] Storage reports effective writable quota and uses complete ZIP sizes for estimates.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] Common pages, contextual Help, per-banner Settings, and scoped Diagnostics follow this standard.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] Yellow/red top-of-page notifications open the exact item Create/Edit/fix flow with scope preserved, keyboard access, and the normal mutation review gates.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] Backend authorization and credential handling are verified; hidden notices do not change capabilities.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] Managed service operation continues during UI/management failure.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] Native release packaging and installation are verified separately from standalone preview/build.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] Repository-owned local interface preview starts and builds using the shared npm workflow.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] Every feature has scrubbed representative scenarios in the repository's global Git LFS demo database/data file; previews consume it through the shared provider.

section: 13. Review checklist for each new plugin
requirement: [ ] `npm run preview` provides usable plugin UI with Docker stopped and without backend, cluster, container-build, or deployment prerequisites.
